$meta.note: The machine-readable path is this FILE, never a docs site (27-F45). Every token carries the FR it answers to. Renames go through `replacement`, never a silent meaning change (27-F39, 27-F46).
$meta.theme: light is the default on every surface; dark is a per-site KDS opt-in (27-F19)

color.$law: 27-F14 allocates 3 status colours + 1 interactive accent PLATFORM-WIDE. A module needing a distinction not on this list uses shape, position or a number (27-F12) — never a fourth hue. Adding one is an amendment to 27-F14, not a local decision. | 27-F19: `value` is the LIGHT theme and is the default on every surface; `dark` is the per-site KDS opt-in. Both sets are gated independently — every 27-F21 pairing and every SC 1.4.11 separation holds in BOTH, so a surface may switch polarity without any component changing.

bgColor-status-confirmed.law: 27-F14 green — TRANSIENT confirmation only, never a resting state

bgColor-interactive.law: 27-F14 blue accent — any control the operator may press

bgColor-inverse.law: 27-F13 — a maximally salient ACHROMATIC surface, for chrome that must be impossible to overlook without spending a 27-F14 status colour. Sole current claimant: the 27-F63 training band. Not a status: inverting is a loudness channel, not a meaning one.

fgColor-on-status-confirmed.law: 27-F43. The dark value is the dark theme's own SUNKEN surface rather than a second near-black: on a dark shell the ink that sits on a bright chip should be a colour the shell already contains, so a chip reads as a hole punched in the surface and not as a foreign swatch. 11.46:1 on the dark confirmed fill.

fgColor-on-interactive.law: 27-F43. Dark takes the theme's own default ink (`fgColor-default` dark) for the same reason as `-on-status-confirmed`, and it is what forced the blue below: pure white on the former #0770FF measured 4.40:1 — under AA, on the one pairing the manifest declares for every pressable control.

fgColor-status-fault.law: 27-F40 — the TEXT form of the fault status. A `bgColor-` token used as a foreground violates the role prefix, whose entire purpose (Primer's words) is to convey which property to use it with.

fgColor-status-abnormal.law: 27-F40 + 27-F21 — the amber FILL (#F0B408) is 1.53:1 against the surface and is unreadable as text. This is the lightest amber that clears AA against EVERY surface token — the first attempt (#A56309) was tuned against the lightest surface only and measured 4.15:1 on the sunken one, which the discipline test caught.

fgColor-disabled.law: 27-F21 — a disabled control still SHOWS ITS REASON, so the reason must stay legible. Opacity is banned for this: fgColor-muted at 0.45 measures 1.88:1, which defeats the whole point of disabling in place. Pair with bgColor-surface-sunken (4.76:1).

borderColor-default.law: 27-F40. SC 1.4.11 at 3:1 — on the light base this border is the ONLY thing separating a tile, key, card or cart from the page behind it, because the neutral fills either side differ by 1.06:1. The former #C7CCD1 measured 1.52:1 against the page and 1.62:1 against a raised fill, so every one of those controls had no perceivable edge. Now 3.41 / 3.62 / 3.14 against surface / raised / sunken. The dark value already cleared the floor (3.44 / 3.00 / 3.87) and is unchanged.

borderColor-strong.law: 27-F40. Re-darkened with `-default`: `strong` must stay STRONGER than `default` or the two names invert, and #8A939D is now the lighter of the pair. 6.14:1 against the page.

outlineColor-status-fault.law: 27-F64 — carries SC 1.4.11 3:1 for its status surface; a lightness derivative of its own fill, never a new hue and never a signal.

space.$law: 27-F41 — FLAT ORDINAL for space, never a semantic gap/inset split. Atlassian shipped five competing spacing schemes at once, including the semantically correct one, and deleted four three days later. 4 px base.

touch.$law: 27-F8 — sizes are POSTURE-typed, never free. A component takes a posture; it does not take a number. The kitchen row sits above the standing-counter minimum on purpose: it is the surface where the 21.34% wet-hand error was measured, read at 1–2 m.

touch-kitchen.posture: standing, wet or greasy hands, 1–2 m

typography.$law: 27-F42 — COMPOSITE tokens only. Decomposed size/line-height primitives let consumers assemble pairings the system never designed. 27-F26: IBM Plex Sans, chosen on fail-safe defaults (tabular digits and distinct I/l with NO feature flags). Roboto is BANNED for numerals. The face is BUNDLED (src/fonts, OFL 1.1) — naming it here delivered nothing until August 2026, when no font file existed in this repo at all. The stack no longer lists system-ui: that resolves to ROBOTO on Android and ChromeOS, so the ban was reachable without the string ever containing the word, which is all the tokens.test.ts guard can see. Android's sans-serif is Roboto too and no stack can fix that — the bundled face is the defence, and layout:check asserts it LOADED.
typography.$family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

text-numeric-display.fontFamily: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
text-numeric-display.law: 27-F25 — "the largest element in THEIR REGION". One step above `text-numeric-hero`, spent only where the region itself is larger: `27-F11c` makes a physically wider panel a bigger region, so a payload held at one size stops being the largest thing in it. NOT a legibility step — 48 dp at arm's length already clears `27-F27`'s 20–22 arcmin comfortably; this is hierarchy, and it is the only place the ladder is spent on room rather than on distance.

text-numeric-hero.fontFamily: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
text-numeric-hero.law: 27-F25 — numbers are the operational payload and the largest element in their region

kds.$law: 27-F27 — KDS type is specified in CAP-MILLIMETRES at a stated viewing distance, NEVER in dp. The same dp renders 2.3× larger on a 32-inch 69-PPI panel than on a phone. Derivation: ISO 9241-303 (20–22 arcmin recommended, 16 minimum) with 30 arcmin for primaries as a safety factor for steam, grease and a moving reader.

money.$law: 27-F23 — `Rs`, symbol-first; Western 3-digit grouping; NO decimals on operational screens. Not ₨, not PKR in staff UI. CLDR gives ur/en-PK the #,##0.### pattern: Pakistan does NOT inherit lakh grouping. 27-F22: Western digits U+0030–0039 everywhere, never U+0660–0669.
